correctness.rationale: For \(n=4pq\), the seven proper unitary divisors are explicitly determined. Equal partition is converted bijectively to a sign equation. The inequality \(q\le5(p+1)/(p-5)<p\) excludes every prime \(p\ge11\). The only remaining primes are \(3,5,7\), and all \(64\) sign triples for each are exhaustively checked by the packaged verifier, including zero-denominator cases. Five surviving prime pairs are each confirmed by an explicit divisor partition. The additional scan through \(q\le1000\) is regression evidence only, not an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The exponent pattern \(4pq\) is the first non-squarefree dyadic three-prime layer where unitary divisors differ from all divisors, so the slice is structurally motivated rather than arbitrary. The result gives a complete infinite-family classification, a sharp bound \(p\le7\), and explicit equal-sum witnesses, extending the focal literature beyond its complete two-prime-support theorem.
